title: Inner product under coordinate identification
statement: For every vector $z$ in the two-dimensional real correlation plane and every vector $t$ in the Euclidean plane, their inner product after identifying the correlation-plane coordinates with Euclidean coordinates is unchanged when the identification is applied to $t$ instead: $\langle z,t\rangle=\langle z,t\rangle$ under these respective coordinate identifications.
hypotheses_covered: $z$ belongs to the real correlation plane
$t$ belongs to the Euclidean plane of dimension two
caveat: The formal statement uses two private coordinate maps whose definitions are included in the payload but have no supplied informal descriptions; the intended identification can be described, but the coordinate-map phrasing is uncertain.
